extracted.intended_audience: science fiction & fantasy writers, readers, and researchers interested in Nebula Award rules and history
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts eligibility, definition, nomination and voting process, and related procedural/history notes for the SFWA Nebula Award for Best Short Story (the annual award for short SF/F under 7,500 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for: The best science fiction or fantasy story of less than 7,500 words published in the prior calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nebula Award for Best Short Story is an annual literary award assigned by the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA). Works longer than 7,500 words are considered in other Nebula categories (novel, novella, novelette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'short story' (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: A work of fiction is defined by the organization as a short story if it is less than 7,500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length thresholds determine category placement; authors should check word counts carefully to ensure correct category entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is for stories published in the prior calendar year (SFWA currently identifies the awards by the year of publication, i.e., the year prior to the year in which the award is given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered for a given Nebula year, a short story must have been published in the previous calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: language and publication venue
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Nebula Award consideration a short story must be published in English in the United States. Works published in English elsewhere in the world are also eligible provided they are released on either a website or in an electronic edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical print publication outside the U.S. may not qualify unless there is an electronic or web edition in English; check SFWA rules for edge cases and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be nominated (authors' membership status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees' authors do not need to be members of SFWA to have works nominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone's eligible work (subject to publication/language/length rules) can be nominated by SFWA members even if the author is not an SFWA member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination period and process (current format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are nominated each year by SFWA members in a period around December 15 through January 31; the six works that receive the most nominations then form the final ballot (with additional nominees possible in the case of ties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After nominations close, members are given about a month to vote on the final ballot; final results are presented at the Nebula Awards ceremony in May.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on self-nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not permitted to nominate their own works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-promotion via official nomination is prohibited; members nominate works by other authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-ballot voting and tie-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the final vote are broken, if possible, by the number of nominations the works received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final voting produces an exact tie, the work with more initial nominations will be favored where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-2009 rules / preliminary ballot process (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the 2009 awards the eligibility period for nominations was defined as one year after the publication date of the work, allowing works to be nominated in a calendar year after their publication and reach the final ballot a year later. Works were added to a preliminary ballot for the year if they had ten or more nominations; that preliminary ballot was then voted on to create a final ballot, and the SFWA organizing panel was allowed to add an additional work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical procedure differs from the current (post-2009) format; historical notes are relevant for understanding past nominations and apparent anomalies in year-labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'No award' option and award refusal / ethics incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'no award' option can win (e.g., in 1970 a 'no award' was selected as the winner), and winners have occasionally refused the award (e.g., Lisa Tuttle refused her award in 1981).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents incidents where voting behavior or contested campaigning (e.g., alleged solicitation of votes) led to disputes; such ethical/contest issues can affect outcomes and have led to withdrawals/refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authored works eligibility / winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners have included co-authors (the historical record notes winners 'including co-authors').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-authored short stories are eligible and may share the award between multiple authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final ballot size (standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard final ballot is formed of the six works that receive the most nominations (subject to ties and any additional tie-handling rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitors should note typical shortlist length (six) when evaluating chances and campaigning (campaigning subject to SFWA rules and ethics).
